title: Foundry Forecasts Domino's Increase in Semiconductor Prices...TSMC Raises Foundry Unit Price By 10% Next Year
source_used: Maeil Business Newspaper (mk.co.kr English edition), citing TrendForce
key_facts: TrendForce said on 5 Oct that suppliers of power-management chips (PMICs), display driver chips (DDIs) and microcontrollers (MCUs) are considering price rises from the end of this year through early next year to reflect higher foundry and back-end processing costs.
Expected increases range from 5% to the double-digit range; foundry costs are the largest share of chip production costs.
TSMC is expected to raise prices again from January 2027; the rise for mature processes is reportedly being discussed at about 3% to 10%, and pricing pressure also continues on advanced processes.

TSMC has reportedly decided to raise 2-nanometer wafer prices by a further 6% to 8% in the first quarter of 2027, citing higher manufacturing and electricity costs; rises of 10% to 20% have reportedly already been applied for individual customers.
Chinese foundries are also considering rises, size not yet set; SMIC, China's largest, earlier raised prices for some high-demand capacity, applying to third-quarter wafers.

Some customers demand supply chains that exclude China, which limits the foundries available for cost cutting; some are bringing orders forward because of Middle East conflict and possible capacity limits from AI demand.
Our 5 Oct edition (C08-07) carried a DigiTimes report, via Technetbooks, of a further 3% to 6% TSMC rise on advanced wafers for the first quarter of 2027.
quote_evidence: TSMC is expected to raise prices again starting in January next year.
The expected increases range from 5% to the double-digit range.
The increase for mature processes is reportedly being discussed at around 3–10%.
why_it_matters_hint: Higher contract chip-making costs are expected to be passed on to the price of everyday power, display and control chips.
event_date: 5 Oct 2026 (TrendForce statement, as relayed by Maeil on 6 Oct 2026)
notes: Follow-up of the 5 Oct edition's C08-07 (TSMC wafer price rise, DigiTimes via Technetbooks). TrendForce's own page was not found, so the credit is Maeil citing TrendForce; the TSMC figures are 'reportedly' with no named source. The 2-nanometer figure (6% to 8%) differs from the earlier 3% to 6% for advanced wafers. TSMC confirmation not stated. The descriptor 'world's largest contract chipmaker' for TSMC is general knowledge, used the same way in the 5 Oct edition's C08-07 entry.
